work.title: Carmen
work.movement: Act II: Escamillo’s couplets — Toreador Song

version.value: Italian-language solo recording, beginning Con voi ber affè mi fia caro, with orchestral accompaniment
version.note: Both verses belong to a self-contained commercial aria side. The stage number’s ensemble responses are not represented as a complete recording of the tavern scene. The Italian translator and the precise performing edition used in the session have not been established.

performers.note: Truesound Transfers identifies the accompaniment and conductor for Victor 88327, matrix C11213-1; the Library of Congress National Jukebox lists the same performers and adds Francis J. Lapitino on harp; Commons identifies the same matrix and singer.

date.note: The year agrees. Commons writes 11 September; the specialist discography prints 09.11.1911 in day-month-year order, meaning 9 November, and the Library of Congress National Jukebox dates the recording 1911-11-09. Only the agreed year is used in the listening header.

place.note: No particular studio address is asserted.

label.note: The recording circulated on several issues; no physical pressing used for the original transfer is identified.

catalogue.note: Victor issue identified by the specialist discography and by the Archive item title cited on Commons.

matrixTakeSides.note: The sources agree on C11213-1 despite their disagreement about the session’s day and month.

credits.value: Original transfer unidentified; noise-reduced restoration uploaded by Adam Cuerden
credits.note: Commons traces its source to Internet Archive item VrsAcoustics-88327-PasqualeAmato. That source item did not return usable metadata when consulted; no original transfer engineer is invented.

date.note: The current restored Ogg was uploaded on 16 January 2009; this is not an established date for the original disc-to-digital transfer.

processing.value: General noise reduction, followed by more selective noise removal
processing.note: The description and revision history document these operations. Stylus, playback equalisation, original sampling format and any pitch correction are not supplied. Commons also links an unrestored version.

digital.format: Wikimedia Commons MP3 transcode of a restored Ogg Vorbis transfer

composition.value: Public-domain nineteenth-century work and historical Italian-language version
composition.note: Commons separately marks the underlying work public domain, using 1908 as the last author’s death year. Bizet’s score was published in 1875. The particular Italian translator is not identified by the recording sources; this is a historical 1911 performance, not a modern translation.

recording.value: Public domain in the United States; Commons marks the commercial acoustic recording as an expired pre-cutoff sound recording
recording.note: Commons explicitly carries PD-US-record-expired and identifies a 1911 Victor recording. The identification is corroborated by the specialist discography. The licence statement does not amount to an assertion that rights are identical in every jurisdiction.

rights.creditLine: Georges Bizet: Carmen, Toreador Song, sung in Italian. Pasquale Amato; Victor orchestra, Walter B. Rogers. Victor 88327, matrix C-11213-1, Camden, 1911. Original transfer via Internet Archive; noise-reduced restoration by Adam Cuerden, Wikimedia Commons. Public domain in the United States.

sources.title: Carmen, vocal score arranged by the composer — Choudens, Paris (archive.org copy catalogued 1883)
sources.locator: No. 14, Couplets, printed p. 128 and pp. 131–143; the digitised copy lacks pp. 129–130. Refrain’s F-major key and ‘avec fatuité’ marking on p. 131; chorus refrain at the close of no. 27, p. 350. The archive catalogues this copy as 1883, described as the 1875 version with certain cuts, not as the 1875 first edition.
